title: EEG: Depression rest
description: Resting-state EEG recordings from 122 college-age participants who scored reliably high or low on the Beck Depression Inventory. Recordings include eyes-open and eyes-closed one-minute blocks, collected in two 6-minute sessions, one after EEG hook-up and one after task performance. The participants overlap with those in the probabilistic selection task dataset, and the data were collected in the Allen lab at the University of Arizona.
methods_description: Resting EEG was recorded circa 2008-2010 in the John J.B. Allen lab at the University of Arizona. The task was programmed in DMDX with instructions alternating one-minute eyes-open and eyes-closed spans (e.g., OCCOCO or COOCOC), marked by triggers. The first 6 minutes followed EEG hook-up and the second 6 minutes followed task performance about 1 hour later. Some files have interpolated channels, and HEOG and VEOG labels may be swapped.
